question: Follow-up to flow-001 (your choice direct_outlets at confidence 0.35, pending). New evidence below separates forced from scripted long balls and measures counter-press spacing. Which defect should be fixed first, and which acceptance criteria are required?

evidence.source: scripts/flow-scenarios.cjs --seeds 3 (docs/engine-qa/flow-baseline.json); clips in docs/flow-clips from the real simulation
evidence.realReference: Approximate top-flight figures, not sourced per metric: direct teams about 60-80 long passes and 25-35 clearances per match with target man plus 2 supporting runners near the landing zone; counter-pressing teams keep the attack compact so 3-4 players can press after a loss; blocks about 30-35 m deep.
evidence.clipObservation: Pressed clearances land in empty space with no direct-side runner following; when the pressing side loses the ball, only 2-3 of its players are near it and the rest are spread 25-40 m away.

newEvidence.source: 8 seeded scenario matches, instrumented decisions of the direct side
newEvidence.cause: sim.js carrierDecide: the clear option has a fixed value (0.02 + pressure*0.05 + deep bonus) that does not depend on any outlet, so under pressure it beats aimed long passes and open short passes; the clearance is kicked to a random spot 30-50% up the pitch, not to the target man.

pressingSideAtLoss.note: A 3-4 player counter-press needs team-mates within about 10-12 m of the loss; at 20 m most counter-presses start isolated.

direct_outlets.summary: Direct side: aimed long balls to the target man or a runner in the channel instead of blind clearances, 2-3 support runners and second-ball midfielders moving to the landing zone, and short escapes when a free man exists (rulebook 9.5).
direct_outlets.tradeoffs: Touches decision scoring for clear/long and off-ball support; may raise the direct side's attacking output.

compact_attack.summary: Pressing side: keep the attack compact around the ball and rest defence in place so 3-4 players are near any loss (rulebook 5.4 steps 1-2).
compact_attack.tradeoffs: Touches attacking shape; may reduce width and change possession numbers.

final_third_marking.summary: Both sides: defenders pick up and track receivers in their own defensive third (box and Zone 14 marking).
final_third_marking.tradeoffs: Touches marking and tracking; may lower chances and goals.

block_compactness.summary: Pressing side: keep the out-of-possession block within 30-35 m (40 m when pressing high).
block_compactness.tradeoffs: Touches line step/drop; may leave space behind.

criteria.clearances: Direct side clearances at most 40 per match and long passes 50-90 per match in the same 24 scenarios.
criteria.support: At least 2.5 direct-side teammates within 15 m of the landing point on average.
criteria.escapes: Short escapes in at least 20% of pressed build-ups.
criteria.counterpress: Counter-presses starting with fewer than 3 nearby players at most 30%.
criteria.marking: Final-third receptions with no defender within 4 m at most 50% for both sides.
criteria.regression: All existing test suites pass, all matches finish with finite positions, zero defensive assignment violations.
criteria.clips: New clips of the same passage types show the change in the real simulation.
criteria.goals: Goals per match between 2.0 and 3.2 (secondary signal only).
